name: Methanosarcina barkeri methanogen (iAF692, genome-scale FBA)

provenance.source: Stumm & Morgan, Aquatic Chemistry (3rd ed., 1996), redox-sequence ladder
provenance.ref: methanogenesis / CO2 reduction sits at the REDUCING foot of the aquatic redox ladder, Eh ~ -400..-200 mV; O2 is toxic to methanogens, so this window is disjoint from any oxic box

notes: A genuinely DIFFERENT organism (second FBA box, first non-E.coli): a strictly anaerobic methanogen. At optimum it consumes methanol + trace nutrients and PRODUCES METHANE (CH4) -- methylotrophic methanogenesis. It can also use H2/CO2 (hydrogenotrophic) and acetate (acetoclastic). Enables SYNTROPHY ecosystems: a fermenter/E.coli produces acetate + H2, the methanogen consumes them -> methane. Shared species (CO2, H2O, H+, ammonium, phosphate, acetate) reconcile with the E. coli box by canonical ChEBI identity + identical BiGG formulas; adds methanol, methane, H2 to the medium.

validity.note: dynamic FBA; strict anaerobe (O2-intolerant). Fluxes mmol/gDW/h-scale.
